trajectory.development: Book 24 is where the labour gap is first met by people rather than by a schedule, and the Special Draw Right's review point is placed there by agent proposal (E7). Both come from agent-proposed elements, so the stage is inferred from them and from the Book 20 arrangement that E1 states.
trajectory.becomes_available: Lineage crews already carry channel repair under the Right from Book 20 (E1), so the labour exists to be asked of others.
trajectory.changes: Changes the Book 20 arrangement in E1 from lineage practice into a question of who gives the labour back before it is owed.
trajectory.quote: Book 24 is where the Long Return's labour gap is first met by people rather than by a schedule.

trajectory.development: A generation that came of age after Book 20 has never seen the labour, and the Brightwater inheritance splits into counted and uncounted practice within one generation. The first claim is derived (E6) and the split comes from E4, whose attribution is unknown_legacy.
trajectory.becomes_available: Lineage crews have carried channel repair under the Right from Book 20 (E1), so the following generation has no sight of the labour.
trajectory.changes: Makes the counted and uncounted split a fact within one generation, so the people asked to give labour back in the first stage do not share one practice.
trajectory.quote: A generation that came of age after Book 20 has never seen the labour, because lineage crews perform it under the Right.

trajectory.development: Proposed: outside apprentices are trained under the Special Draw Right and their repair is shown, so the Right's training condition is tested. The record states the condition (E7) but not that training happens; this assumes training can occur in a later development.
trajectory.becomes_available: The Right is conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage (E7), and the maintenance lineages say they need that condition demonstrated (E3, an agent inference).
trajectory.changes: If training is shown, the condition is met in the story rather than only stated; if not, the Right is exposed, and the Book 24 review point tests a condition that is unmet.
trajectory.quote: The Special Draw Right is conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage.

trajectory.development: Proposed: the public capability record that Book 24 exports is used to show who can repair, so repair is seen per person and not only counted. The export is an agent-proposed element (E5); its use is not in the cited items.
trajectory.becomes_available: Book 24 exports a public capability record, separate from debt, tally and aggregate balance (E5, agent-proposed).
trajectory.changes: Gives the counted and uncounted practice a record of who can repair, which may change how the within-generation split reads; whether it does is not stated in the cited items.
trajectory.quote: exports one new kind of record: a public capability record, separate from debt, tally and aggregate balance

trajectory.development: Conditionally, and inferred from the hypothetical E8: the cohort practising both counted and uncounted return may claim standing in how the valley coordinates channel work. Book 24 names no body to grant it; whether later Books take up the question is not stated in the cited items.
trajectory.becomes_available: A cohort that practises both counted and uncounted return (E8, hypothetical; the split is in E4).
trajectory.changes: If the claim is made, channel coordination gains a claimant, and Book 24 names no body that would grant that standing (E8).
trajectory.quote: may claim standing in how the valley coordinates its channel work

relations.reason: The thread already asks who performs the return labour (E1), and the first stage is where that gap is first met by people; the link is thematic, not one the later stage cannot occur without.
relations.quote: Who performs the return labour that keeps the spring balanced, and at what cost to families with few hands.

relations.reason: The review point and the training condition both concern the Right; the cited items do not say the review cannot occur before training, so this is helpful only, not a prerequisite.
relations.quote: The Special Draw Right is conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage.

relations.reason: If the Brightwater practice splits within one generation (E4, unknown legacy attribution), the people asked to give labour back do not share one practice, which complicates the gap being met by a single group.
relations.quote: The Brightwater inheritance splits into counted and uncounted practice within one generation

relations.reason: A public record of who can repair might bear on standing, but E8 mentions no record; this link is an assumption of the synthesis and is not stated in the cited items, so it is preparation only.
relations.quote: exports one new kind of record: a public capability record, separate from debt, tally and aggregate balance

alternative_paths.ordering: Book 24's labour ask stays with the existing lineage crews, and no outside apprentices are shown, so the review tests the training condition only as stated.
alternative_paths.effect: The training stage drops out and the condition stays stated rather than demonstrated; the Right is exposed on the record's own terms.
alternative_paths.quote: they need the condition demonstrated or the Right is exposed

alternative_paths.ordering: The training condition is shown before the review point is taken, so the review tests a demonstrated condition rather than a stated one.
alternative_paths.effect: Keeps the training stage ahead of the review; the source's reversal for the review point (E7) could still reverse it, so whether this stays viable is unresolved.
alternative_paths.quote: the source gives a reversal for it

alternative_paths.ordering: The capability record is not exported in Book 24, so the record stage drops out.
alternative_paths.effect: Standing for the cohort then rests on nothing recorded; E8 mentions no record, so standing is not shown to need one, and the stage stays conditional and viable.
alternative_paths.quote: exports one new kind of record: a public capability record, separate from debt, tally and aggregate balance

opportunities.text: Proposed: a public record of who can repair could let the counted and uncounted practice of one generation read as differing capability rather than a split; neither the record nor the split makes that possible alone.
opportunities.quote: that says who can repair rather than who

opportunities.text: Proposed: if outside apprentices are trained, the labour the thread names could move from lineage crews toward households that can meet the rota; neither the thread nor the training condition makes that possible alone.
opportunities.quote: households that can meet the rota carry the rest

reader_experience: Book 24 gives the labour gap, a generation that has never seen the labour, and a record that says who can repair; the later stages are proposed or conditional and are not presented as arriving. Book 25 repeats five Book 24 texts (E9-E13 match E3-E7), so it adds no second view of these stages.
open_decisions: Whether the Special Draw Right's review point stays in Book 24, given the source's reversal noted for it.
Whether outside apprentices are shown on the page, or the training condition stays only stated.
Whether the public capability record bears on standing for the cohort, or stays separate from it.
Which body, if any, would grant the cohort standing; Book 24 names none.
uncertainty: The reversal the source gives for the review point (noted in E7) is not in the cited items; the review point's placement is an agent proposal.
E5 and E11 are excerpts cut off mid-sentence; what the capability record says after 'rather than who' is not in the cited text.
E9-E13 repeat E3-E7 in Book 25, and E4 has unknown legacy attribution, so the counted and uncounted split rests on an unattributed element.
Whether any later Book asks the standing question is not stated in the cited items; E14 covers eleven citing elements for the thread, all excerpted, in Books 24 and 25.

criticism_assessments.reason: E5 and E7 are attributed agent_proposed, and E7 itself calls the review point agent-proposed as P1, so the labour-gap stage is relabelled inferred, not recorded, and states how it follows.

E8 is hypothetical and says only that the cohort may claim standing; the stage now keeps that conditional and drops the claim that Books 24 and 25 do not ask the question, which is not stated in the cited items.
E8 mentions no record; the record appears only in E5. The enabling link is replaced by a preparation link whose premise is marked as an assumption, not stated in the cited items.

E7 makes the Right conditional on training and places the review point in Book 24, but does not say the review needs training first. A prerequisite overstates that dependence, so the link becomes preparation with thematic dependence.

changes_from_prior: Stands: the Book 24 labour gap, the generation without sight of the labour, and the Right's training condition, as the cited items state them. The labour-gap stage is now inferred, not recorded.
The standing stage keeps 'may claim standing' conditional and drops the claim that Books 24 and 25 do not ask the question; that absence is not stated in the cited items.
The prerequisite link between the review point and training becomes preparation with thematic dependence; the record makes the Right conditional on training, not the review dependent on it.
The enabling link from the capability record to standing becomes a flagged preparation link, since the standing element mentions no record; the reversal noted in E7 is now an open uncertainty.
